source.title: Large Batch Training Does Not Need Warmup
source.authors: Zhou-Yuan Huo; Bin Gu; Heng Huang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether large-batch training and recipe changes affect held-out performance, using large-batch optimizer and warmup comparisons rather than the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The study reports large-batch experiments relevant to V5. Its mentions of generalization gaps and sharp minima in the introduction cite prior work and are not its own results. The layerwise learning-rate experiment reports training-loss convergence, not a result on the claim’s generalization gap.
record.test_reason: Figure 2 directly compares held-out image-classification accuracy across batch sizes under a fixed 200-epoch budget, testing V5 with an adapted training recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that CLARS removes the need for warmup in their experiments and converges faster than LARS with warmup on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet; they also report better ImageNet test error. They do not establish that CLARS closes a small-versus-large-batch accuracy gap.
record.recipe_differences: Compares LARS batch-size scaling and a newly proposed optimizer, CLARS, including warmup versus no-warmup conditions; it does not reproduce the original large-batch generalization-gap studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size and optimizer/warmup recipe; results are reported for CIFAR-10 and ImageNet models, with different epoch budgets and learning-rate settings.

fits_no_version.finding: At batch 8192, CLARS without warmup outperforms LARS with 5-, 10-, or 20-epoch warmup during 20-epoch CIFAR-10 runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing the large-batch optimizer can improve early held-out accuracy without warmup; this comparison does not measure the effect of batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: At effective batch 16384, CLARS converges faster and reportedly achieves better test error than LARS on ImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CLARS can improve large-batch optimization and held-out performance relative to LARS at the same batch size.

record.code_released: https://github.com/tensorflow/models/blob/master/official/resnet/resnet_run_loop.py (official implementation followed for ImageNet setup; study code release not stated)
record.problems: The held-out accuracy comparisons are presented in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The 200-epoch batch-size comparison uses LARS with 20-epoch warmup, so it does not isolate batch size from the adapted training recipe.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported held-out results on batch-size scaling were found beyond the CIFAR-10 comparisons recorded. ImageNet Figure 5 compares CLARS with LARS at batch size 16384, but does not compare large versus small batches and therefore does not directly measure V5's batch-size penalty.

Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance; Figure 1 measures training-loss convergence instead.
Adaptive methods versus SGD under limited and broader tuning.

Language models; batch-size sweeps with an unadapted recipe; longer-training remedies; isolated contributions of warmup, learning-rate scaling, normalization, and regularization; batch-size thresholds beyond the tested CIFAR-10 range.

Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Accuracy effects of removing memorized training examples.

record.verdict_notes: An absent penalty in R1–R2 supports the adaptation clause already included in V5. R3–R4 cannot support a V5 verdict because both methods use the same large batch. No precise accuracy values or uncertainty estimates are available in the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: ResNet56
rows.operation_detail: Trained with LARS, gradual warmup and polynomial learning-rate decay while scaling batch size.
rows.measure: Top-1 testing accuracy and convergence rate
rows.note: The text says the convergence rates for the tested batch sizes are similar and that accuracy may improve as batch size increases; precise values are only in the figure.
rows.check: The large-batch penalty is qualitatively absent under the adapted LARS recipe: Section 4.2 reports similar convergence across batches 128–8192 and possible accuracy improvements. Replace partial; exact final accuracy differences cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text. Convergence speed alone should not be treated as generalization.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.operation_detail: Trained with LARS, gradual warmup and polynomial learning-rate decay while scaling batch size.
rows.measure: Top-1 testing accuracy and convergence rate
rows.note: The text describes similar convergence rates across the tested batch sizes and says accuracy improvements may be observed; precise values are only in the figure.
rows.check: The large-batch penalty is qualitatively absent under the adapted LARS recipe, according to Section 4.2's summary of Figure 2. Replace partial; exact final accuracy differences cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.

rows.subject: ResNet56
rows.operation_detail: Compared CLARS without warmup with LARS using gradual warmup.
rows.note: Authors state CLARS outperforms LARS with gradual warmup by a large margin; the plotted accuracy values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: This compares the proposed CLARS method against LARS at one batch size. Better testing accuracy at batch 8192 does not establish a batch-size penalty or its removal relative to smaller batches.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.operation_detail: Compared CLARS without warmup with LARS using gradual warmup.
rows.note: Authors state CLARS outperforms LARS with gradual warmup by a large margin; the plotted accuracy values are not stated numerically.
rows.check: This compares the proposed CLARS method against LARS at one batch size. There is no smaller-batch control establishing V5's effect.

relationships.condition: ResNet56 and VGG11 on CIFAR-10, batches 128–8192, 200 epochs, LARS with linear learning-rate scaling, 20-epoch warmup, and polynomial decay.
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 qualitatively support V5's adapted-recipe exception: Section 4.2 reports similar convergence and possible accuracy improvements as batches increase. Exact endpoint differences are unavailable.
relationships.display_finding: The study reports similar convergence and possible accuracy improvements with larger batches, but the comparison remains unverified and exact endpoint differences are unavailable.
